amendments.normalized_body: In `affects_habitat_registry()` (actions.rs:159-169), `ChangePhotoperiod` is listed as affecting the habitat registry, but the habitat computation in `compute_habitat_registry` reads `hardware.light.intensity_index` not `hardware.light.photoperiod_hours`. Photoperiod changes produce a redundant registry refresh. Either remove `ChangePhotoperiod` from the match, or add a code comment explaining the deliberate over-approximation so future maintainers don't second-guess it.

The legacy `total_colonizable_area_cm2()` (biology.rs:660-669) used by `algae_growth.rs:167` computes colonizable area as `wall_area_cm2 + substrate_layers.colonizable_area_cm2`, which omits `geometry.hardscape_area_cm2`. Now that hardscape area is a configurable field on `TankGeometry`, adding hardscape to a tank increases habitat registry `GlassHardscape` area but the algae carrying-capacity model ignores it entirely. Add a note (doc comment or inline TODO) clarifying this omission so the downstream habitatization task (tanksim-6e5.5.3) knows to migrate algae to the habitat registry rather than the legacy helper.

crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:731-755, crates/tank_core/src/types/substrate.rs:24-36, and crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:220-225 do not actually derive SubstrateDeep area from current geometry. Scenario materialization stores colonizable_area_cm2 as footprint * factor (depth is ignored), the default layer hardcodes 100.0 cm², and the habitat registry then trusts that stored scalar verbatim. Two beds with the same footprint but different depths therefore get the same deep-substrate area, and TankState::new() reports the same 100 cm² regardless of tank size. That breaks the "geometry-derived colonizable area" contract for the habitat that downstream redox/biofilm systems are most likely to depend on.

crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:117 and 204-215 compute SubstrateSurface.light_exposure from geometry.mean_depth_cm(), and crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:60-62 defines that as fill_height_cm. Substrate thickness is therefore ignored: a shallow bed and a deep bed in the same tank get the same substrate-surface light even though the top of the deeper bed sits much closer to the lamp. The bead explicitly calls out depth/light context, so this misses one of the required sensitivities for the substrate habitat.

crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:85-94 derives avg_crowding from the stored plant.crowding_index values, but crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:608-649 trims plant biomass without updating crowding, and crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:217-219 refreshes the habitat registry without recomputing crowding from the new biomass/footprint. After a large trim, PlantSurfaces area drops immediately but GlassHardscape/SubstrateSurface light exposure stays over-shaded until the next daily plant update. The registry is therefore still stale with respect to a plant-driven modifier even though it was just "refreshed."
